description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources in the combined training dataset used for evaluating attribution by large language models, as referenced in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” The chart is divided into 13 distinct segments, each representing a different data source, with percentages indicating their relative contribution. The largest segment is NQ (Natural Questions), accounting for 31.3% and colored blue. The second largest is FEVE (likely a dataset abbreviation), at 16.7%, shown in teal. SNLI follows with 15.4% (orange), and MULTINLI contributes 11.3% (red). VITAMINC makes up 13.0% (light blue), while PUBHEALTH is minimal at 0.5% (light green). Other sources include SCITAIL (1.2%, yellow-green), SUMHUL (1.6%, gray-blue), SCIFACT (0.1%, dark yellow), ENTFA (1.8%, dark green), FACTCC (2.6%, olive), and ANLI (4.6%, orange-red). A small unlabeled segment near the bottom appears to represent TIEC or a similar source, though its percentage is not visible. The chart uses a legend-style labeling with lines pointing to each slice, and percentages are displayed next to most labels. The segments are arranged in roughly descending order of size, with the largest (NQ) positioned at the top right. No slice is exploded or emphasized visually beyond its proportional size.
